MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  DECEMBER 13, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:10 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Technician/Code Administrator Jessica Slawson

Others Present:  Pam Schachter, Park and Activities Commission
  Tim Thomas, Planning Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PRESENTATION TO OUTGOING MAYOR STEVE ZUCKERMAN

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted his pleasure in recognizing the City’s
  accomplishments under MAYOR ZUCKERMAN’S leadership. He also thanked
  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN for his many years of service on the COUNCIL and
  presented him with a gavel.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted his appreciation for MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN’S comments and thanked the COUNCIL and staff for working so
  well together for the benefit of the community.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 15, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY  COUNCIL  MINUTES  OF
  NOVEMBER 15, 2016 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57728 THROUGH 57763 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $116,178.51; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110116 THROUGH 110216;
  57506 (VOID); 57565 THROUGH 57585; 57648 THROUGH 57663; 57664
  (VOID); 57665 THROUGH 57714 IN THE AMOUNT OF $687,791.79 FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $803,670.30 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
DECEMBER 13, 2016
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-F.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

B.  OCTOBER 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  OCTOBER MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  BUDGET AMENDMENT FY 2015-16 AND 2016-17

  APPROVED THE FUND CLOSURE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2015-16 AND THE
  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2016-17.

E.  SEMI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  BUSINESS LICENSE REVISIONS

  DIRECTED STAFF TO INCLUDE THIS ITEM FOR DISCUSSION AT THE
  MARCH 2017 POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO NOMINATE MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN AS THE CITY’S NEW
  MAYOR BY ACCLAMATION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO NOMINATE COUNCILWOMAN HUFF AS THE CITY’S NEW MAYOR
  PRO TEM BY ACCLAMATION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked the COUNCIL MEMBERS for their support and
  commented that they are “amazing public servants.” He further noted his
  appreciation of his role as an elected official and reflected on his feelings of being
  an American because he has been given so much in contrast to everything that
  was taken away from his family in Armenia. In providing background on his
  heritage and his position as a teacher all over the world, he stated that it gives
  him an opportunity to express the greatness of America. Finally, he noted that it
  is his hope to maintain and enhance the culture of his Armenian heritage.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 13, 2016
   ***
  At 7:25 p.m., MAYOR ZERUNYAN called for a brief recess.
  ***
  At 8:03 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened with MAYOR ZERUNYAN, MAYOR
  PRO TEM HUFF, COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, COUNCILWOMAN
  SCHMITZ, and COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN present.

  ***

8.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  Martin Gombert, Administrator, PV Transit, announced that they will offer free
  shuttle service to Peninsula residents from 6:00 p.m.-2:00 a.m. on New Year’s Eve
  and reservations can be made beginning December 22. He further noted that an
  advertisement will be broadcast on Channel 33 and brochures will be available
  next week.

9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 712

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION 1.12.010 OF CHAPTER 1.12
  (ELECTIONS), AMENDING SECTION 2.04.020 OF CHAPTER 2.04 (CITY
  COUNCIL), AND ADOPTING PROCEDURES TO CONSOLIDATE ITS MUNICIPAL
  ELECTIONS WITH STATEWIDE JUNE ELECTIONS PURSUANT TO SENATE
  BILL 415 BEGINNING IN 2018, AND TO EXTEND THE TERMS OF EXISTING
  COUNCILMEMBERS AS A RESULT OF THE MANDATED CHANGE IN THE
  CITY’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION DATE.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, City Manager Prichard noted that
  the Policy Development Session will still be held in March.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  No public testimony was offered.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING AND CONTINUE TO THE NEXT
  MEETING FOR SECOND READING AND ADOPTION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 712 by title only.

10.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 21, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 21, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 13, 2016
 B.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 5, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 5, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

11.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 711 SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 1.25 OF THE
  ROLLING  HILLS  ESTATES  MUNICIPAL  CODE  PERTAINING  TO
  ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 711.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 711 by title only.

B.  RESTATED EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the restated employment
  agreement with the City Manager.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE RESTATED EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT WITH THE
  CITY MANAGER.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  E-MAIL RETENTION POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the proposed E-Mail Retention
  Policy.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  City Manager Prichard noted that staff communication with the COUNCIL will
  now utilize only their City email addresses on any business-related matters.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT THE PROPOSED E-MAIL RETENTION POLICY.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

12.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  BEST PRACTICES FOR USE OF SOCIAL MEDIA BY CITY OFFICIALS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report and direct
  that this memorandum be sent to all Commission Members, Committee
  Members and Staff Members.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 13, 2016
   Brief discussion ensued regarding posting of City events on Facebook versus the
  City’s website.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT AND DIRECT STAFF TO SEND THE
  MEMORANDUM TO ALL COMMISSION MEMBERS, COMMITTEE
  MEMBERS AND STAFF MEMBERS.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

13.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that she enjoyed chairing this committee. She
  thanked Community Services Director Clark and City Manager Prichard for their
  assistance in working with her on the various items that have come forward.
  Finally, she wished to recognize the good work this committee does.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 24, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN reported that the Sanitation Districts is looking to
  possibly build a new main line out to the ocean.

C.  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN mentioned that the City of Rancho Palos Verdes is
  reviewing their relationship with the Fire Department in an attempt to
  determine the amount residents pay for services on the Peninsula. City
  Manager Prichard noted that he will keep the COUNCIL apprised of any
  developments.

14.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT  CITIES
  LEGISLATIVE ORIENTATION TOUR – JANUARY 9-11, 2017

  After brief discussion, the COUNCIL authorized those who wished to attend this
  conference: MAYOR ZERUNYAN, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, COUNCILWOMAN
  SCHMITZ and COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN.

  It was noted that the regular COUNCIL meeting of January 10, 2017 will be
  cancelled.

15.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 13, 2016
 16.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:55 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 13, 2016
